profile.headline: Staff Software Developer in Biosystems Data Science at the Berkeley Lab
profile.summary:
I integrate and analyze biomedical datasets: unstructured text to relational databases. Recently, that has taken the form of semantic modelling, at the individual and class level. I gravitate towards notebook computing and reproducible research tools like RStudio, iPython/Jupyter, R Markdown/knitr, and Shiny.

Most recently, I was involved in semantic modeling of Penn's Electronic Health Records. I have also worked in drug safety informatics, industrial biotechnology, infectious diseases and therapeutic protein expression.  My contributions include genomics analyses; providing bioinformatics training; installing, maintaining  and modifying web-based bioinformatics tools created by others; and leading a team that created a web-based tool for comparing proteomics results.

I have been  active in vaccine discovery, pain research, immunotoxicology and tumor biology/tumor immunology  laboratories. Previously, I had a very enjoyable career in all phases of LC/MS proteomics and flow cytometry approaches, from experimental design,  sample preparation, instrument operation and maintenance, to interpretation of results.

positions.title: Principal
positions.description: Informatics, data integration & visualization, especially gene expression, pathway analysis, and metagenomics.

positions.title: Biomedical Ontologist
positions.description: Authoring and applying ontologies like OBI ( http://obi-ontology.org/page/Main_Page ) for applications like biobanks.  Part of the TURBO team:  http://upibi.org/turbo/

positions.title: Bioinformatics Application Consultant & Product Manager
positions.description:
In additional to ongoing ad-hoc bioinformatics analyses, construction of two automated, production components of Instem's KnowledgeScan Target Safety Assessment product:

1) Genomics analyses, grouped by organ system.  Input data types include gene expression, comparative genomic analyses between human and lab species, phenotypic analyses of mouse knockouts and human variants, such as SNPs.

2) Comprehensive identification of synonyms for drug targets and construction of PubMed corpora specific to the target.  Synonym discovery starts with a very broad scope and transparently filters based on specificity and ambiguity.

Built a virtual appliance version of the SRS application (life sciences data integration)

Management of post-sales relationships with 20 customers from international pharma, biotech, agriculture and universities.  Dotted-line management of technical staff on customer projects.  Management of relationships with upstream vendors and business partners.

positions.title: Staff Associate Investigator
positions.description: Bioinformatics application support and development for projects including biofuels, biomaterials, and agricultural trait enhancement.  Creation of value-added protein diversity networks.  Quantitative comparison of microbial communities with QIIME.  Administration of and training for web-based data interfaces.

positions.title: Senior Bioinformatics Scientist
positions.description: Compartive genomics and functional genomics support for Vaccines Research, Infectious Disease Research and microbial bioprocesses.  Maintained a mirror of JCVI's excellent Comprehensive Microbial Resource and integrated it with other commercial or bespoke bioinformatics tools.  Used a SGE-based High Performance Computing environment for quick execution of multi-genome homolgy comparisons, etc.

positions.title: Research Biologist
positions.description:
Used LC/MS proteomics and bioinformatics for vaccine target identification and validation.

Prior to that, spent about 2.5 years operating a flow cytometry/cell sorting facility for Molecular Pharmacology/Pain Research.  Also operated a confocal microscope and laser scanning cytometer.

patents.title: Using alkyl hydroperoxide reductase as tool in developing vaccines to prevent and treat microorganismal infection; immunotherapy
patents.description: The present invention features polypeptides comprising an amino acid sequence structurally related to SEQ ID NO: 1 or a fragment thereof, S. aureus AhpC-AhpF compositions, and uses of such polypeptides and compositions. SEQ ID NO: 1 has a full length S. aureus AhpC sequence. A derivative of SEQ ID NO: 1 containing an amino His-tag and three additional carboxyl amino acids was found to produce a protective immune response against S. aureus.

patents.title: Polypeptides for inducing a protective immune response against staphylococcus aureus
patents.description: The present invention features polypeptides comprising an amino acid sequence structurally related to SEQ ID NO: 1 [SACOL0912] and uses of such polypeptides and compositions thereof. SEQ ID NO: 1 is a full length S. aureus sequence. A derivative of SEQ ID NO: 1 containing an amino terminus his-tag was found to produce a protective immune response against S. aureus.
